thread:
maria: Heads up — seeing ~18 nodes in eu-west-2 stuck in PROVISIONING after the OOB BMC fw push at 03:10 UTC. They never finish PXE because eth0 link training keeps failing. :eyes:
aj: ugh. Is it limited to a single rack or spread?
maria: spread across two racks (rack-b and rack-c). All are GPU pools, 8x A100s each. Provisioner shows the nodes as 'firmware-hold' and `oobctl` prints continuous `link training retry` in the console. Logs below:
```
[2026-03-18T03:12:02Z] oob: node-evb-12 eth0: link training failed (partner does not respond)
[2026-03-18T03:12:02Z] bmc: secureboot=enabled last_change=2026-03-18T03:09:58Z
[2026-03-18T03:12:05Z] provisioner: node-evb-12 state=FIRMWARE_HOLD reason=eth0_link_training_retry
[2026-03-18T03:14:11Z] kernel: pcie0: rate drop detected, reinit pending
```
samir: did the push toggle secure-boot or change signing keys? That can trigger a revalidation handshake on the BMC side and sometimes irritate NIC firmware.
maria: not intentionally. Release notes said "BMC 2.3.4: improved serial multiplexing and minor nic stability fixes" — no secure-boot line. But the `bmc` logs show a secureboot attestation event around the same time.
kelsey: @maria can you paste the `oobctl show node-evb-12` output? I want to confirm iBMC runlevels.
maria: pasted snippet:
```
$ oobctl show node-evb-12 --json
"state": "FIRMWARE_HOLD",
"bmc_fw": "2.3.4",
"last_event": "secureboot_attest_start",
"eth0": {"link": "down", "link_retries": 47}
```
aj: for immediate mitigation, can we mark those nodes as maintenance so autoscaler releases capacity or fails over? We need to avoid PGs being queued in prod.
oncall: I've set the infra tag `maintenance:oob-firmware-hold` on the 18 nodes and drained the GPU pools for new scheduled jobs. :white_check_mark:
deploy-bot: rollback job queued for bmc-fw rollforward -> target 2.3.3 on subset applier `eu-west-2-rack-b` (canary) :hammer:
samir: before rollback — could the NIC firmware have negotiated a lower link width because of a microcode change? If so, firmware rollback might not clear the secureboot attestation state. We should attempt a BMC soft-reset + force re-run of NIC microcode load on one node as a canary.
kelsey: agreed. maria — can you run `oobctl reset-bmc --soft node-evb-12 && oobctl run-nic-init node-evb-12` on a canary and paste output? Keep me in the loop.
maria: running now. output:
```
$ oobctl reset-bmc --soft node-evb-12
OK: soft-reset issued (watch logs)
[30s later]
oobctl run-nic-init node-evb-12
OK: nic init started; firmware image 1.4.7 loaded; link training: SUCCESS
provisioner: node-evb-12 state=PROVISIONING
```
maria: canary recovered after soft reset + nic-init. Others still flapping.
aj: good sign. That suggests microcode load order/timing got jostled by the fw push. Rollback still seems prudent for the bulk — but do we have capacity implications/commitments for Dedicated customers in eu-west-2 if we start mass reboots?
maria: we have a reserved pool for dedicated; I'm flagging Finance because mass reboots will drop capacity for ~20m per node.
oncall: suggestion: stagger rollback in 4 waves, 6 nodes per wave, apply soft-reset + nic-init preflight. That should keep capacity impact contained.
samir: also add a quick health-check script to console-steps that asserts `eth0 link training success` and `secureboot state == attested` before marking ready. Prevents future race.
kelsey: I'll add the check to the provisioner canary pipeline after rollback waves.
aj: timeline?
maria: starting wave 1 in 10m on rack-b. Will report back. :rocket:
maria: wave 1 done: 6 nodes soft-reset+nic-init -> all healthy, PROVISIONING -> READY.
maria: wave 2 started.
deploy-bot: rollback wave 2 scheduled (6 nodes) -> apply 2.3.3 at 03:45 UTC.
maria: wave 2 done. wave 3 in progress. 2 nodes in wave 3 showing `secureboot_attest_timeout` — escalating to hw-vendor.
samir: opened vendor ticket P-2026-1947, included logs and link-training captures. ETA 4 hours.
kelsey: good call. Adding temporary route rule to route new provisioning requests to eu-central while we finish waves to reduce customer-facing queuing.
aj: thumbs up. Keep the comms short: we should post a short incident note in #incidents if customer impact > 5m.
maria: will draft after we finish rollback. current status: 14/18 recovered, 4 in vendor triage.
oncall: tagging with `oob-fw-fix` and adding to runbook. :page_with_curl:
maria: thanks all. follow-up: we'll add microcode init ordering to the next fw rollout checklist and require NIC-init smoke before completing the push. :memo:
